method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across attentive perception of the world, the seeker’s inward dispositions, reading beneath the words of scripture, visions, symbols and the life of the spirit, revelation and the unveiling of hidden mysteries, wisdom in what is disclosed and withheld, what lies beyond this life, understanding that becomes service and prayer, and further voices on wonder and discernment. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: On the Day of Manifestation, the trumpet was sounded and the bugle was blown. Both the assured and the doubtful were gathered together, but the assured one awakened and became conscious, became aware of death and life, crossed over the bridge, and entered the paradise of sanctification. But the heedless remained unaware of both death and life, and "they perceive not when they shall be raised."
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s account of the Day of Manifestation in which the assured awakened while the heedless remained unaware of death and life; contrasts perception and heedlessness.

selected.text: A spiritual fragrance is wafting toward the souls--that is, from the gardens of the Abha Kingdom holy breathings are being diffused and the nostrils of the people of Paradise are stirred and perfumed. This fragrance bestoweth life and conferreth eternal existence.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s description of a spiritual fragrance from the Abhá Kingdom that confers life; sustains the guide’s imagery of fragrance.

selected.text: O falcon of the heaven of the love of God! Now is the time for flight and the discovery of divine mysteries.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s brief address to a falcon of the heaven of the love of God that now is the time for flight and the discovery of divine mysteries; a vivid image of the present as the season for discovery.

selected.text: O thou who wanderest in the wilderness of signs and swimmest in the seas of mysteries! How canst thou be perplexed when thou art like a fish in the depths of this sweet and flowing sea? By thy life! If for a moment thou wouldst turn thy gaze toward the Kingdom of God from which the gates have been opened, the glad-tidings of the Glorious Lord would seize thee and the melodies of that matchless Garden would attract thee with such power that thou wouldst rend thy garments and tatters, cast off all restraint, and cry out: "Hasten to witness the Unseen made manifest! Hasten to the water that hath been poured forth! Hasten to the support that hath been granted! Hasten to the glorious station beneath this raised standard and under this outstretched shade!"
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s address to one perplexed in the seas of mysteries, likened to a fish in a sweet sea, urging a turn toward the Kingdom; a vivid answer to perplexity.

selected.text: Thou art a servant of the divine threshold and art fully aware of the mystery of spiritual truth. Strive with all thy power in prayers and communions at the hour of dawn to increase thine alertness day by day, to strip away the misgivings that veil the people of doubt and lead them towards the Most Great Guide with the potent knowledge of God so that like unto a candle thou mayest illuminate every meeting with the light of recognition.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to one aware of spiritual truth to pray at dawn, grow in alertness and guide others so as to illumine every meeting; turns awareness into service.

selected.text: Open the eye of insight and behold the light of truth. The effects of the outpourings of the Abha Kingdom have encompassed the hidden world and the universe. … And when thou discoverest such an outpouring rain and fountain of mysteries, say: "Glorified, Holy is the Lord of the angels and the Spirit!" … The eye of the Ancient Beauty's loving-kindness is open, and His grace and bounty encompass every free servant
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to open the eye of insight and behold the outpourings of the Abhá Kingdom encompassing the hidden world; a direct exhortation to perceive grace already present.

selected.text: Wander and roam in this endless desert, and in this destination of the people of knowledge, seek your dwelling and abode. Drink from the living waters from the spring of certitude, and from this tree of certitude pluck the fruit of the highest heaven. The door of bounty is open and the glad tidings of the invisible Kingdom are continuous and successive. When you reach the shore of the sea of life, fill your skirt with the pearls from the shells of grace, so that those brilliant jewels may shine forth in the crowns of existence.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s invitation to drink from the spring of certitude and fill one’s skirt with pearls on the shore of the sea of life; a vivid image of the seeker’s gathering.

selected.text: With a detached heart, an attracted spirit, and an enkindled soul, burning with the fire that was ignited on Mount Sinai, seek the outpourings of the Spirit from all directions. Verily I say unto thee, the mysteries of the divine Spirit will be unveiled to thee, thy radiant heart will be stirred, and thou wilt say: "Praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds!"
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s promise that a detached heart and enkindled soul seeking the outpourings of the Spirit will see the mysteries of the divine Spirit unveiled; joins detachment and attraction.

selected.text: The mystery of servitude is revealed when the light of the Divine Identity shines forth upon the world of the heart and the lamp of reality is kindled within the inner chamber of the soul. When its radiance touches the tongue, utterance becomes the essence of Divine Unity, and when its rays fall upon the pillars of being, there proceed such deeds, actions, ways, conduct and behavior as constitute the very life of existence. And when it casts its effulgence upon the realm of minds, the mysteries of the seen and unseen become manifest.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s explanation that the mystery of servitude is revealed when divine light shines in the heart, issuing in utterance, deeds and the mysteries of the seen and unseen; links mystery to conduct.

selected.text: This is the Day in which the Beloved Who declared "Thou shalt not see Me" now proclaims "Look and thou shalt see Me."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the Beloved who said “Thou shalt not see Me” now proclaims “Look and thou shalt see Me”; a memorable reversal for this Day.

selected.text: So, when one is spiritually developed, a sublimity of nature is obtained, a delicacy of vision such as could not otherwise be found.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that spiritual development brings a sublimity of nature and a delicacy of vision; links perception to growth.

selected.text: The time hath come for thee to witness all the signs within thine inmost being and to observe all the signs in the universe in every atom
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to witness the signs within one’s inmost being and in every atom of the universe; joins inner and outer perception at the start of the guide.

selected.text: Mrs. Harrison asked what was the cause of the sensation often experienced by both of us which felt as if an essence were falling upon the top of the head, and a sensation flowing down around the face and on into the heart (she mentioned Aaron's beard)--also like irrigation. Was it merely a physical sensation? Imaginary? Or wrong? … 'Abdu'l-Baha: "No it is not a physical condition, but spiritual, a very high one which is so intense it reaches the nerves and these react upon the body
selected.reason: Reported question and answer in which ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes a sensation felt by two believers as spiritual rather than physical; a reported personal experience kept with its own status.

selected.text: I have journeyed through the unseen worlds and invisible realms of the Almighty collecting New Thoughts, New Conceptions, New Proofs and New Evidences.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá about journeying through the unseen worlds gathering new thoughts and proofs; a personal statement kept as reported speech.

selected.text: The Blessed Perfection has revealed a Tablet called 'Tablet of the Spiritual World.' All who read it are filled with an anxious desire to leave this world and enter the next condition, so wonderful are the gloriesof the Spiritual Kingdom. In Persia, one man who read this Tablet killed himself. he could not wait for the happiness it promised him. Another, a youth of Isfahan, could not stand the spiritual food contained in this Tablet, and lost his reason
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that readers of Bahá’u’lláh’s Tablet of the Spiritual World were filled with longing for the next world, with two extreme cases; retained as a reported anecdote within the discussion of concealment and capacity.

selected.text: For I am with thee wherever thou dwellest; that place is overflowing with spiritual susceptibilities, and the light of the Kingdom casteth its effulgence upon it.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s assurance that he is with the believer wherever they dwell and the light of the Kingdom shines upon that place; a note of fellowship.

selected.text: Remember the days when thou wert present before the Countenance and didst witness what no eyes have witnessed throughout ages and centuries, and didst hear what no ears have heard.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s reminder to one who stood before His Countenance and witnessed what no eye had witnessed; a narrative of encounter with the Manifestation.

selected.text: even though they were unaware thereof, they were like unto the fish of the deep, which are immersed in the sea without knowing it, and are beneath the gaze of the Concourse on high.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of believers like fish of the deep immersed in the sea without knowing it; a gentle image of unrecognized grace.

selected.text: There is a station destined for man that if he reaches to it, he will find all the created phenomena holding conversation with him; he will see that everything is speaking with him.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that at a certain station all created things seem to converse with a person; returns to the world perceived anew.

selected.text: The fragrance of the garment of Joseph bestoweth life anew upon the Jacob of desire, and the delicate savours of the divine rose-garden delighteth the mystic nightingale that warbleth amid its blooms.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of the fragrance of Joseph’s garment reviving the Jacob of desire and delighting the mystic nightingale; a scriptural image of recognition.

selected.text: Therefore, O knower of mysteries, strive that people may gain the insight of the righteous and become manifestations of the favors of the Lord. May they open another eye to witness the Divine Spirit.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s charge to a knower of mysteries to help others gain insight and open another eye; turns insight toward others.

selected.text: it is hoped that through divine assistance you will emerge from the bewilderment you mentioned and enter the paradise of holy unveiling and witnessing, and arrive at the city of certitude and assurance
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s hope that divine assistance will bring a bewildered seeker into the paradise of unveiling and witnessing and the city of certitude; addresses perplexity on the path.

selected.text: I swear by the Ancient Beauty that the effects of the Greatest Name will become so manifest and evident in the soul and conscience, even in bone and flesh, that the mind will be bewildered and confounded.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s oath that the effects of the Greatest Name will become manifest in soul, conscience and even bone and flesh; shows mystery reaching the whole person.

selected.text: On the Day of Splendor you opened the eye of insight and beheld the lights, penetrated the Kingdom of mysteries and pondered the signs, becoming aware of the hidden truth and the veiled reality.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words to one who opened the eye of insight on the Day of Splendor and became aware of the veiled reality; a personal confirmation of insight.

selected.text: May they become the soaring heights of mystical knowledge and privy to hidden mysteries. May they become the breeze of the rose garden of divine unity and the manifestation of the favors of the Glorious Lord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer that the friends become heights of mystical knowledge and the breeze of the rose garden of unity; joins knowledge and unity.

selected.text: O Lord! I was sleeping when the breeze of Thy Day of Manifestation stirred me. When it awakened me, it inspired me with that of which I was heedless in Thy days. O Lord! I caught Thy fragrance and hastened unto Thee.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer of one awakened by the breeze of the Day of Manifestation and inspired with what he had been heedless of; a personal image of awakening.

selected.text: You have caught the fragrance of Joseph's garment and discovered the divine Egypt, and like Jacob you have gained seeing eyes. I hope that you may behold the divine Joseph's countenance and attain the station of unveiling.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words to one who has caught the fragrance of Joseph’s garment and gained seeing eyes like Jacob; a scriptural image of restored sight.

selected.text: When I awoke, I felt that the Spirit of God had permeated and taken possession of My soul. My heart was thrilled with the joy of His Divine presence, and the mysteries of His Revelation were unfolded before My eyes in all their glory.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Moses beheld a blazing Fire from the verdant Tree and heard a Voice. He fell unconscious and became the confidant of the celestial Herald and Angel. He brought forth the manifest serpent and drew forth the white hand from the mighty bosom.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s retelling of Moses beholding the Fire in the Tree, hearing the Voice and bringing forth signs; the prophetic model of encounter.

selected.text: not the world of the womb, when compared with this world, but as illusions and dreams? Even so is this earthly life but illusion when compared with the life hereafter. When man passed from the world of the womb into the world of sense, the veil was lifted from before him, the covering removed, and he perceived that which in the world of the womb he had neither comprehended nor could
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s comparison of this life to the world of the womb, whose veil is lifted at birth; the foundational analogy for what lies beyond this life.

selected.text: At that moment there came from the direction of the Most Exalted Paradise a breeze from which I detected the fragrance of the Beloved, and through it I came to know what none in the worlds had known, and I found what none among the mystics had found.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s account of a breeze from the Most Exalted Paradise through which He came to know what none had known and found what no mystic had found; a first-person narrative of disclosure.

selected.text: Thus have the channels of allusion, like ships in motion, coursed upon the sea of contingent beings, that the countenance of love might become visible from all created things, and the essence of affection might appear within the realities of all mentioned things
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of channels of allusion coursing like ships upon the sea of contingent beings so that the face of love becomes visible in all things; a memorable image of allusion.

selected.text: Ye have heard the harmony of the Supreme Concourse and listened to the glad songs of the nightingale of the orchard of guidance, ye received a share and a portion from the heavenly Food, and became associates and partners in the outpouring of the Kingdom of Abha!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words to believers who have heard the harmony of the Supreme Concourse and received a share of the heavenly Food; a communal picture of spiritual reception.

selected.text: Souls who are prepared are like candles, coming in contact with fire. They become illumined. They are swayed by the wafting of a breeze. They become green and verdant from a drop of the sprinkling of the cloud of favor. They find merciful susceptibilities by hearing a word.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening prepared souls to candles lit by contact with fire and plants made verdant by a drop of rain; illustrates receptivity.

selected.text: Whosoever truly attaineth unto this most exalted station and most glorious horizon, the hidden mysterious manifestations and the veiled maidens of inner meanings from every direction without direction and from every station without veils will be unveiled and revealed unto him.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that one who attains this station will see the veiled maidens of inner meanings unveiled from every direction; a striking image of inner meanings.

selected.text: While engulfed in tribulations I heard a most wondrous, a most sweet voice, calling above My head.  Turning My face, I beheld a Maiden -- the embodiment of the remembrance of the name of My Lord -- suspended in the air before Me.  So rejoiced was she in her very soul that her countenance shone with the ornament of the good pleasure of God, and her cheeks glowed with the brightness of the All-Merciful.  Betwixt earth and heaven she was raising a call which captivated the hearts and minds of men.  She was imparting to both My inward and outer being tidings which rejoiced My soul, and the souls of God's honoured servants
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Ye are clinging to the hem of grandeur and are wanderers in the path of the Abha Beauty. … This is bounty upon bounty, and this door of hope hath been opened before the face of all the peoples of the world. Yet some are privy to these mysteries while others are deprived of this bestowal and supplication
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s observation that though the door of hope is open to all, some are privy to these mysteries while others are deprived; notes the difference in reception.

selected.text: Having inhaled the fragrances of divine mysteries within the signs of their own hearts, and having become that Bird of Truth soaring in the eternal realms of the Concourse on High … they witness at every moment the endless outpourings of God, the All-Glorious, within their heart, soul, spirit and body
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s description of souls who inhale the fragrances of divine mysteries within their own hearts and witness endless outpourings in heart, soul and body; locates the mysteries within.

selected.text: For the holy melodies of the spirit a new ear is needed, and for the fragrances of the paradise of the soul an exalted heart is required, and for the wondrous divine knowledge an illumined heart is befitting, so that with heavenly assistance through these spiritual means one may perceive the gems of divine wisdom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the melodies of the spirit need a new ear and divine knowledge an illumined heart; names the inward faculties that perception requires.

selected.text: If thou openest the eye of thy soul and gazest upon the Kingdom of the Best-Beloved, thou wilt observe that this is a letter of liberation whereby thou shalt gain admittance to the divine Kingdom, and when thou takest flight from this dusty realm of darkness to the luminous world, thou shalt hasten to the private chamber of the Truth
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that a letter is one of liberation and that leaving this dusty realm leads to the private chamber of Truth; links death and disclosure.

selected.text: It is morning and the lights of the bounty of grace are shining and gleaming from the invisible Kingdom of the Most Glorious Realm. Pure hearts are receiving endless divine manifestations and hidden outpourings, while successive glad tidings from the unseen world arrive and holy fragrances spread from the gardens of oneness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s morning image of pure hearts receiving endless divine manifestations and hidden outpourings; a fresh image of continuing grace.

selected.text: Praise be to God that thy heart hath become the Valley of the sacred Mount, and thy breast the Sinaic plain. The flame of light hath been kindled, and the mount of heart and soul hath become illumined and radiant. Thou hast heard the divine call and from the sacred Mount hast hearkened to the melody of "Thou shalt not see Me."
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that a believer’s heart has become the Valley of the sacred Mount and has heard “Thou shalt not see Me”; turns the Sinai story inward.

selected.text: When it reaches the chamber of sight, the mysteries of the Kingdom are witnessed. When it reaches the window of hearing, the call to wakefulness and awareness from the Abha Kingdom and the anthem of glorification from the Concourse on High are heard. When it rises from the horizon of the brow, the radiance of the All-Merciful is manifested.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of a light reaching the chambers of sight and hearing so that the mysteries of the Kingdom are witnessed and its call heard; a vivid account of inward senses.

selected.text: God hath, through His bounty and grace, removed the covering from off thine eyes and inspired thee the night in which the Morn of Guidance dawned and the Holy Spirit breathed in the being of "The Exalted, the Supreme". Ye went out, desirous to witness and visit the Lord, and awaited the appearance of the Great Bounty in that brilliant night.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s words that God removed the covering from a believer’s eyes and inspired him on the night the Morn of Guidance dawned; a narrative of a visionary awakening.

selected.text: While We were seated upon the throne, there entered a radiant leaf, clad in fine white raiment, appearing as the full moon rising from the horizon of heaven. Exalted be God Who created her! No eye hath ever seen her like. … When she lifted her veil, the heavens and earth were illumined as though the Ancient Essence had shed upon her its splendors
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s Tablet of the Vision describing a radiant leaf whose unveiling illumined heaven and earth; a primary visionary text kept with its own identity.

selected.text: Verily I have seen the Kingdom of God with its doors open, the garden of El-ABHA with extensive sides and regions, with dazzling lights, rolling seas, verdant and beautiful orchards, overflowing beds, green trees, fresh and bright leaves, perfumed flowers, sweet rivers, gentle breeze, beautiful air, magnificent views, elegant and handsome lips and mouths
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s account of having seen the Kingdom of God with its doors open and the garden of Abhá in luminous detail; a vivid visionary description.

selected.text: thou who hast turned unto the world of the Kingdom! At this moment, as I sit by the Sea of Galilee, detached from all save the Friend, and expectantly awaiting the universal outpourings of the All-Merciful, I have taken up my pen to write this brief letter. If you but knew the state in which I write, you would surely be moved to ecstasy and rapture, and in the excess of your joy and yearning you would dance as you sang this verse: "Whence comes this musician? What
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writing by the Sea of Galilee of a state that would move the reader to ecstasy; a personal narrative of rapture within the visions section.

selected.text: Verily the exquisite chalice hath overflowed with the choice wine, and verily the delicate glass hath sparkled with the luminous lamp, and verily the manifest horizon hath been illumined by the brilliant, radiant star, and verily the precious necklace hath been adorned with rubies and unique pearls, and verily the sweet, flowing river hath surged with mighty waves.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s sequence of images of an overflowing chalice, a sparkling glass and a surging river; a lyrical evocation of the abundance of the Day.

selected.text: Journey in the land of wonder and of mystery and travel far and wide within the realms of power in order to behold the proofs and signs of God. Open thou the eye of true discernment so as to see for thyself the blazing fire kindled on Sinai, and open the ear of truth that thou mayest hearken to the call of the divine Beloved summoning thee from the Supreme Horizon.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s summons to journey in the land of wonder and mystery and open the eye of discernment to see the fire of Sinai; an invitation to wonder that frames the guide’s first section.

selected.text: Wert thou to discover what hath been ordained for thee in the Most Glorious Kingdom, thou wouldst spread the pinions of longing and grow the plumes of yearning, and soar unto the Supreme Companion. However, the all-encompassing divine wisdom hath required the concealment of this magnificent bounty and ancient generosity, lest every heedless blameworthy one covet it.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that if the reader saw what is ordained for him in the Kingdom he would soar, but wisdom conceals this bounty; the complete form of this passage.

selected.text: I ask God that He may open the gate of the knowledge of these stations to thine heart so that thou mayest apprehend whatever is necessary and proper, garner spiritual bounties from the heaven of the All-Merciful, obtain the effulgences of knowledge from the Sun of Reality, and become a manifestation of inspiration from the Unseen and a source of glad-tidings from the All-Merciful.
selected.original: I ask God that He may open the gate of the knowledge of these stations to thine heart so that thou mayest apprehend whatever is necessary and proper, garner spiritual bounties from the heaven of the All-Merciful, obtain the effulgences of knowledge from the Sun of Reality, and become a manifestation of inspiration from the Unseen and a source of glad-tidings from the All-Merciful. selected.reason: Authorized words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asking God to open the gate of knowledge to the heart, so that the reader may obtain the effulgences of the Sun of Reality and become a manifestation of inspiration from the Unseen; a prayer for understanding among the closing readings.

selected.text: Pure and transparent souls, which were clear from the rest of matter, immediately became enlightened and luminous and reflected the lights upon the world of contingent beings. This effulgence, to those pure hearts, was like unto a Call, a Revelation, a Splendor and Hearer by music. Therefore each one acquired a special effulgence and made manifest and apparent a certain Divine Glory.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s description of pure souls receiving divine effulgence as a call, a revelation, a splendor and music, each manifesting a special glory; shows diversity of spiritual experience.

selected.text: Praise be to God that like unto a torch thou hast been ignited, and like unto a star thou hast shone. This light is the light of reality, which is divine guidance, and not a material one. It is a heavenly lamp and not an earthly one which, although it reveals objects, yet it does not discover and comprehend them, i.e., it is unaware of the world of things, and simply reveals them to the eye; while on the other hand, the light of Truth both reveals and discovers objects and does moreover comprehend them. … Praise be to God that thou hast attained to such a light
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s distinction between material light that only shows objects and the light of Truth that reveals, discovers and comprehends them; a memorable image of knowing.

selected.text: Spiritual disclosures are of two kinds: One, which is commonly referred to among other peoples, is mere imagination, while the other is true spiritual visions such as the revelations of Isaiah, of Jeremiah, and of John … In like manner, spiritual disclosures are of two kinds. One is the visions of the Prophets and the spiritual disclosures of the chosen ones of God. The visions of the Prophets are not dreams but true spiritual disclosures
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: As for what thou asked regarding the state of the spirit and its conditions, know of a certainty that the dream world is equivalent to the spirit and like unto the sun in its station; nothing hath departed from the body.  Nay rather, by its light whatever is in the heavens and the earth may be witnessed.  Were a devout believer enabled to see all things by this divine agency, still would he reap the fruit of his belief, and naught can alter it; and were an unbeliever enabled to see all things upon the reflected forms, still on account of his unbelief
selected.reason: The Báb’s answer comparing the dream world to the spirit like the sun, adding that a believer enabled to see all things would still reap the fruit of belief and an unbeliever of unbelief; qualifies the value of visionary sight.

selected.text: When the veils of the elemental world and the dark curtain of this earthly realm are lifted from sight, the vast expanse and broad space of the divine world becomes manifest, and the Beloved of divine bestowals unveils His face, and the gifts of the All-Merciful become evident. One sees the gates of the Kingdom opened and finds the breasts of the dwellers of the realm of might expanded. The realities of mysteries become manifest and the subtleties of lights become apparent.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s description of the divine world becoming manifest when the veils of the elemental world are lifted; a vivid picture of what lies beyond.

selected.text: Open an eye unto the Most Glorious Kingdom and become privy to His mystery, and harmonious with His holy fragrances, that ye may behold the Most Great Sign and taste the honey of faithfulness and spread the wings of knowledge and soar in the infinite space.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to open an eye to the Kingdom, become privy to His mystery and spread the wings of knowledge; a compact image of insight leading to flight.

selected.text: As for the unveiling of the beauty of the Holy Manifestations at the time of ascending to the limitless worlds, this pertaineth to the fact that the world of physical senses and material perceptions is metaphorical while the world of the spirit is reality itself. When the morning of reality dawneth, the realities of all created things will become apparent, the heedless will become conscious, the slumberer will awaken, and they will behold the Manifestations of Truth clearly and unmistakably. "We have removed from thee thy veil, and thy sight is sharp this day."
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s explanation that the beauty of the Manifestations is unveiled at death because the spirit’s world is reality itself; a substantive explanation of unveiling after death.

selected.text: We are ignorant; suffer us to become informed with Thy Mysteries.
selected.reason: Reported prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá: We are ignorant; suffer us to become informed with Thy Mysteries; a humble petition.

selected.text: Guard thou the mystery of God, for it was made manifest in the year sixty.
selected.reason: The Báb’s brief charge to guard the mystery of God made manifest in the year sixty; connects mystery to the historical moment of revelation.

selected.text: Without divine civilization the mysteries of the Kingdom are not revealed
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that without divine civilization the mysteries of the Kingdom are not revealed; ties discovery to social life.

selected.text: I beseech Thee by the mysteries of Thy knowledge which none hath known save Thee
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s petition by the mysteries of God’s knowledge which none has known save Him; keeps the closing linked group and its humility.

selected.text: Know then the allusion, for it has been sent down from behind seventy thousand veils
selected.reason: The Báb’s brief counsel to know the allusion sent down from behind seventy thousand veils; a memorable image of the distance of symbolic speech.

selected.text: when a man is taught the mystery of God, his eyes are opened but his lips are sealed

selected.reference: (provis. trans. from a Tablet of Baha'u'llah, in Safiniy-i-'Irfan, vol. 12, pp. 16-17)
selected.text: As the Law of Generosity enacted upon all who are in the heavens and on earth hath been set to the level of their comprehension and rank, know thou that unto the wayfarer who journeys to God and migrates to Him, detaching himself from this transitory abode, seeking to ascend to the eternal home, shall be revealed hidden mysteries and well-guarded truths; The essence of unity and the manifestations of eternal might shall appear to him. And if he arrives at that most exalted station and transcendent home it behooveth him to be entrusted with the treasures of the knowledge of God, and to be the keeper of the pearls of His wisdom. It behooveth the wayfarer to guard this knowledge deposited in the receptacles of enlightened hearts by God the creator of mankind, to protect it as his eyes, and to conceal it in his breast. Were he to reveal one letter of these secrets other than to those who are worthy, he shall have perpetuated three serious crimes. The first is betrayal inasmuch as he hath betrayed God by exposing His mysteries to those unsuited to hear them. The second is injustice inasmuch as he conferred this station upon one who doth not deserve it, and weighed him down with an unbearable load he cannot carry. Therefore the verdict of oppressor hath been pronounced upon such a wayfarer; and what oppression can be greater than this? The third is murder because he misled this wretched one and killed him by killing his faith, inasmuch as he was unable to comprehend this divine knowledge, his feet slipped from whence he had progressed in the Cause of his Origin and Return. Therefore it can truly be said of him that he has been killed, and the punishment for such shall be imposed upon his killer.

selected.text: This other and inner reality is called the heavenly body, the ethereal form which corresponds to this body. This is the conscious reality which discovers the inner meaning of things, for the outer body of man does not discover anything. If the outer material body did this, the animal would, likewise, be able to make scientific and wonderful discoveries, for the animal shares with man all physical powers and limitations. It is the inner reality which comprehends things, throws light upon the mysteries of life and being, discovers the heavenly Kingdom, unseals the mysteries of God and differentiates man from the brute. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference (Pilgrim notes of Hooper Harris, 1907, in SW v15#05 p.133) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, a pilgrim’s account attributed to Hooper Harris, reports that ‘Abdu’l-Bahá wrote to him to turn with his heart to the heart of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá so that hidden mysteries would be revealed, that he obeyed and the mystery was revealed but could not be expressed in words, and that it is no mystery to those who met ‘Abdu’l-Bahá heart to heart. The quoted Tablet wording is not verified. No authority is asserted; keep on merit as a reported personal account.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference (St. Augustine, Confessions 11.9.11) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, attributed to St. Augustine’s Confessions 11.9.11, describes something that flashes upon and pierces the heart without wounding, making him shudder inasmuch as he is unlike it and burn inasmuch as he is like it, and names it Wisdom itself rending the cloud around him. It is a comparative text outside the Bahá’í Writings. No authority is asserted; keep on merit as a comparative perspective.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference LG#1845 (8 Dec. 1935 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied elided extract, written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, states that the core of religious faith is the mystical feeling uniting man with God, maintained through meditation and prayer, that believers should cultivate spirituality chiefly through prayer, and that the Bahá’í Faith, like all divine religions, is fundamentally mystic in character. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference LG#1723 (29 Nov. 1929 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, says that writers like Emerson were inspired by God, but that their tendency to seek communion by looking within and to treat the Prophets as humans whom we can equal diminishes the Prophet’s position and makes religion the religion of the few who have experiences. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; no supplied reference (the extract names Albert Einstein) and not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, attributed in its own text to Albert Einstein, calls the mysterious the most beautiful thing we can experience and the fundamental emotion at the cradle of true art and true science. It is a comparative text outside the Bahá’í Writings with no source given. No authority is asserted; keep on merit as a comparative perspective.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference (6 May 1952 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, quoted here) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, states that true and significant visions occasionally come through the grace of God and not through any human faculty, that they should not be sought or developed, and that striving to develop such faculties weakens spiritual capacities and can destroy character. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference Plotinus, Enn.VI.7.26 not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied extract, attributed to Plotinus, Enneads VI.7.26, argues that pleasure is not self-sufficient and that one who takes the feeling of attaining the good for the good itself remains empty. It is a comparative text outside the Bahá’í Writings and does not address mystery, vision or discernment directly. No authority is asserted; omit on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference LG#1742 (25 Oct. 1942 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied elided extract, written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi, states that truly mystical experiences based on reality are very rare, that groping in the darkness of imagination after them is dangerous, and that God will vouchsafe a deeply spiritual experience without our looking for it. No authority is asserted; keep on merit.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference (St. John of the Cross, Ascent of Mount Carmel, book II, ch. II) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. The supplied elided extract, attributed to St. John of the Cross, Ascent of Mount Carmel, says that supernatural representations to the bodily senses must never be relied on but fled from, since the senses are ignorant of spiritual things and esteeming them exposes one to deception and impedes spirituality. It is a comparative text outside the Bahá’í Writings. No authority is asserted; keep on merit as a comparative perspective.

importedAuthorityReview.authorization: No catalogue record; supplied reference (St. John of the Cross, Letter XI) not verified against an official text in this review.
importedAuthorityReview.finding: No candidate catalogue record. It is a comparative text outside the Bahá’í Writings. No authority is asserted; keep on merit as a comparative perspective.
